newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli planes hit Lebanon after Hizbollah attack.
newsitem.headline: Israeli planes hit Lebanon after Hizbollah attack.

text.p: Israeli planes struck three times in Lebanon on Monday after Hizbollah guerrillas wounded four pro-Israeli militiamen and an Israeli soldier in an attack in the south, security sources said.
The planes attacked suspected Hizbollah targets in the hills of Mleeta in a rugged south Lebanon mountainous area after nightfall, Lebanese and pro-Israeli militia sources said.
In Jerusalem, an Israeli army spokeswoman said: "Israeli warplanes this evening attacked terrorist targets in the Jabel Safi area in the eastern sector of south Lebanon."
"The pilots reported accurate hits on the targets and all the planes returned safely to base," she added.
Earlier in the day, Israeli planes rocketed the nearby hills of Sojoud and Akmata, the sources in Lebanon said.
There were no reports of casualties in the attacks that raised the number of Israeli air raids on Lebanon in 1997 to 28.

The attacks came after four South Lebanon Army (SLA) militiamen and an Israeli soldier were wounded in fighting with Hizbollah guerrillas who stormed into the outpost of Sojoud on the edge of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, the pro-Israeli sources said. Israel confirmed the casualties.

This brought to 28 and 22 respectively the number of Israeli soldiers and SLA militiamen wounded in guerrilla attacks since the start of the year. Six Israeli soldiers and five SLA members were killed over the same period.

There were conflicting reports about the number of Hizbollah guerrillas killed in the attack -- ranging from one according to the pro-Iranian group itself to four according to an Israeli army spokesman.
SLA sources said two Hizbollah guerrillas were killed near the entrance of the outpost after planting flags on the position.
In Beirut, Hizbollah said one of its fighters, Hussein Bahij Nasser, was killed in the operation.

"The group of April War Martyrs stormed into the outpost of Sojoud where the group of Qana Martyrs advanced and blew off the implanted barriers causing a hole in the outpost's defences," a Hizbollah statement said.

"Simultaneously, the group of Mansouri Martyrs opened a similar hole on another side of its fortifications. In great speed, the two groups infiltrated into the outpost and cleared it with rocket-propelled grenades, machineguns and explosive bombs."
Hizbollah guerrillas regularly attack Israeli troops in an attempt to oust them from the south Lebanon occupation zone, which Israel says protects its northern border.
